correctness.rationale: Writing s=k+gamma, the exact coefficient identities MC/L=gamma b, MD/L=-(gamma-1/2) C, ME/L=(1-gamma)D cancel the s^-1, s^-3/2, and s^-2 defects. The remaining local defect is O(s^-5/2). Monotonicity and L=||M|| give ||B_s||<=sqrt((1-gamma/s)^2+1/s)=1-(gamma-1/2)/s+O(s^-2), hence the claimed contractive propagator. Its discrete convolution yields O(s^-3/2 log s) for gamma=2 and O(s^-3/2) for gamma>2. The independently expanded instantaneous Tikhonov resolvent has second coefficient -gamma^2 L^2 M^-2 b, giving nonzero lag gamma L^2 M^-2 b/2. Exact-rational testing of 416 cancellation/lag identities and 36 finite-trajectory assertions corroborates the calculations. The proof applies to arbitrary finite-dimensional nonnormal invertible monotone real M; the numerical checker is not presented as a proof.

value.rationale: The signed nonzero gamma L^2 M^-2 b/(2s) discrete-to-Tikhonov tracking discrepancy is a natural invariant of a published anchoring method and informs second-order bias/calibration. The vector residual limit proves that its generic O(s^-1/2) worst-case scale cannot be improved for the fixed schedule even on strongly convex quadratics, while an invertible skew bilinear saddle lies in the same theorem. These are substantive asymptotic method-specific limits; the claim does not advertise a universal lower bound for other algorithms.
